name: Chain of Strength
label: Revelation
lede: Chain of Strength put out two seven-inches in about three years. Ray Cappo signed them after hearing a demo in Ryan Hoffman's car, and the clothes drew as much argument as the songs.

eras.title: Signed from a car stereo
eras.text: Southern California straight edge mostly borrowed its look and sound from Boston and New York. Chain of Strength wanted the heft of the Cro-Mags with the melody of Dag Nasty, and on the day of their first show, Ray Cappo heard the demo and asked to put it on Revelation.

years.h: Chain of Strength wants Cro-Mags heft and Dag Nasty tunes
years.p: Curtis Canales sings, Frosty (Paul Hertz) and [[Ryan Hoffman|22c60d75-ef91-4601-8467-2fd06b67842d]] play guitar, [[Alex Barreto|9e81a640-5c20-444e-9064-d2d65cf87328]] plays bass and [[Chris Bratton|cbaf85ca-1bc7-4eb0-b9cb-ca5d8773b27f]] plays drums. Frosty says Hoffman called around 1987 to get it started.
years.xp: Bratton came in fresh from [[No for an Answer|23d26104-95e2-473f-a704-ab0bcd702da3]] and [[Justice League|550a452b-26f6-4ba8-993d-7b8fbf1f691f]].

years.src: RevHQ Speak Up: Ryan Hoffman · No Echo
years.h: Ray Cappo hears the demo in Hoffman's car before the first show
years.p: Hoffman and a friend booked the Yesteryears show in Pomona themselves, with Chain of Strength opening. [[Ray Cappo|e8357f9d-f7f5-4858-a766-aef004bb38a6]] of [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]] heard the tape that day and asked for it.
years.xp:
The bill: [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]], [[Insted|3677d0cb-dd2e-472e-b92b-f64cec75ddb4]], [[Underdog|de38fbd3-7155-497a-bf3c-1a8db3091859]], [[Soulside|de2e8176-32c2-4abe-b718-9392dffd8ffe]], [[Hard Stance|3029fc29-bf7c-4f78-8bfc-97c0bf144c6d]], [[Bold|b024b1bd-2020-4b7c-83f7-4660133c89fa]], and a brand-new Chain of Strength on the bottom. Those bands happened to be touring at the same time. Cappo's line to Hoffman, per RevHQ, was "I want this on Revelation," and Hoffman said yes on the spot.

Frosty remembers it a little differently: they played it for Cappo and [[Porcell|dff848b4-bb79-445a-81e1-3db65b7ddd3e]], who were like, "Yo, Revelation right now!"

Hoffman says what made the day last wasn't the offer. It was the do-it-yourself show and the friendships, the San Diego crew among them, that started in that room.

years.h: Connecticut gets Chain of Strength first, at the Anthrax
years.p: The Anthrax bill also had [[Judge|3827fbb6-e219-4e2d-9af8-35cc9a7d8d8e]] and [[Alone in a Crowd|1639f026-7a51-4762-a3f4-53a10353f4a8]]. Revelation's own bio lists the band's early shows with [[Gorilla Biscuits|0320a32e-b781-40df-bf48-5cb5ee842762]], [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]], [[Bold|b024b1bd-2020-4b7c-83f7-4660133c89fa]], [[Social Distortion|e1e05cce-3922-44e1-8f20-015abe5e309d]] and the [[Cro-Mags|9ffa627f-32c2-4cb1-bfad-00cf348abc70]].

eras.title: Dressed nice, and made to answer for it
eras.text: Two seven-inches came out, the second on Hoffman's own label. The band also cared how it looked, and plenty of people in hardcore had opinions about that.

years.src: No Echo · RevHQ Speak Up: Ryan Hoffman · Wikipedia
years.h: True Till Death comes out as Revelation No. 10
years.p: The demo Cappo heard in Hoffman's car went out as-is, because the master tape had been lost. The first press came on green vinyl.
years.xp:
It was cut at Spot Recording in Orange County, where a lot of local bands recorded. The vocals sit low in the mix, a leftover from the demo. Frosty wrote most of the two-chord title track.

Frosty counts Chain as only the second West Coast band on Revelation, after [[No for an Answer|23d26104-95e2-473f-a704-ab0bcd702da3]], at a time when the label was almost entirely a New York story.

The UK got both seven-inches through First Strike Records, a Wigan label run out of a skate shop.

years.cap: Chain of Strength at Fenders Ballroom, Long Beach, August 1989
q: We liked to dress nice. So what?
years.h: Stussy, mock turtlenecks and a lot of flak
years.p: Chain of Strength dressed sharp: bleached and shaved heads, rolled cuffs, a look cribbed from Boston's SS Decontrol and [[DYS|f012c04d-96ca-47dd-9359-3bb11fed88b5]]. Critics called it fashion.
years.xp:
"We got a lot of shit for wearing Stussy, mock turtlenecks," Frosty told No Echo. His answer was that the band just liked to look good.

Bratton later described the Youth Crew uniform as white and black Nike high-tops, athletic sweatbands and a grown-out shaved head, bleached blond.

years.h: Live at Fender's Ballroom, Long Beach CA, August 4, 1989
yt: Live at Fender's Ballroom, Long Beach CA, August 4, 1989

years.cap: Chain of Strength at Spanky's Cafe, Riverside, around 1989-90
years.h: Hoffman starts Foundation Records with What Holds Us Apart
years.p: Not on Revelation this time. Gang vocals come from a crowd of scene friends, and the songs turn toward betrayal inside hardcore itself.
years.xp: Frosty's explanation: Revelation was rad, but they wanted their own label, and Hoffman had started Foundation.

years.h: Too many side projects end Chain of Strength
years.p: Chris Bratton is drumming for [[Inside Out|0049c4d7-6459-4b54-a865-fd19969f427f]] with [[Zack de la Rocha|aa659468-db56-41c9-b6fe-61f4bb2ef1a6]], and Alex Barreto, who'd drummed in Inside Out's early days, goes on to start Statue. An EP's worth of new songs never gets recorded.
years.xp:
The last show was at Raji's in Hollywood on June 8, 1991, and someone filmed it. Frosty says the breakup came down to everyone being in so many projects.

He has described the lost material as Subject to Change by [[Faith|f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574]] meets [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]]'s Out of Step. The band later called the breakup kind of traumatic.

eras.title: Both records, one sleeve
eras.text: Both seven-inches had gone out of print and kids kept asking. Revelation put everything on one record, and the band's catalog has been in print ever since.

years.h: The One Thing That Still Holds True puts both seven-inches on one record
years.p: Revelation's compilation gathers True Till Death, What Holds Us Apart and one song nobody had heard, eleven tracks in all, on CD, LP and cassette. The 12" followed in 1996.

eras.title: Twenty-four years later, Irving Plaza
eras.text: Revelation's 25th birthday got the five of them back in a room. Two New York nights turned into Los Angeles, a Washington church and a festival in Quebec, with a newer generation of bands on the same bills.

years.cap: Chain of Strength at Rev25, Irving Plaza, New York, October 12, 2012
yt: True Till Death, Rev25, Irving Plaza
years.h: Rev25 puts all five of Chain of Strength back on stage
years.p: Their first shows since the breakup, on Revelation's 25th anniversary weekend: Irving Plaza in New York on October 12 and 13, plus a Brooklyn show at Acheron.
years.xp: "Exactly 24 years to the week, we returned to that same little rehearsal studio to play our first show together since breaking up," the band told Vice.

years.cap: Chain of Strength at Rev25, Irving Plaza, New York, October 13, 2012
years.h: The first interview in 20 years spends its time on clothes
years.p: Vice gets the band on record, and Chris Bratton's point is that you could play hardcore without a punk costume of leather and spikes.
years.xp: Bratton called the Youth Crew look "just as codified, specific, thought out, and detail orientated, as any Mod ensemble Steve Marriott and Paul Weller ever slaved to get perfect."

years.cap: Chain of Strength at Destroy LA, The Vex, Los Angeles, July 13, 2013
years.h: The reunion comes home to Los Angeles
years.p: Chain of Strength plays Destroy LA at the Vex on July 13, back in Southern California where it started.

years.h: Chain of Strength and Turnstile share a church in DC
years.p: A short run with [[Turnstile|7b748dac-f5ce-45a7-9b95-c1d8b5b013ed]], [[Strife|5e911223-4228-4a14-8f6c-7d2dfeb62530]], Mindset and Praise: the D.C. church on June 14, Acheron in Brooklyn the next night, Anchors Up in Haverhill on June 18.

years.h: Quebec's Amnesia Rockfest books Chain of Strength with Blink-182
years.p: The poster in Montebello also lists [[Mötley Crüe|26f07661-e115-471d-a930-206f5c89d17c]] and [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]].
years.xp: Brooklyn Vegan described the church and club dates as the warm-up for the festival, which had more than 80 acts, among them Weezer, Alice in Chains, Megadeth and Primus.
